prereqs
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```


## Intro

This document is a place for process for creating the Santa Barabara Code pipeline. 

## Reading in the data

There were two different file types provided for the Santa Barbara Corpus- .trn and .cha. I decided to use .trn files since they seemed to read in more naturally as a data frame. 

```{r}
trn_df <-  read_delim(file, col_names = FALSE)
#reads in a single trn file and lets R decide the column names
```

Originally, I named the columns. However, I later realized that some of the files had different delimiters which changed the number of columns as a result from 3 to 4. To fix this, I simply let R named the files and incorporated a [if else]() statement for dealing with this discrepency.

## Cleaning the text

The next step was to create a function called `clean()` that would clean each line of the transcript. This process started with identifying symbols that were not part of the actual dialogue and then figuring out what they meant. I listened to audio versions of the first .trn file to get a sense of any transcription markings I wasn't familiar with. Ultimately, I ended up with the following function for cleaning the lines. 

It was necessary to create two functions inside of `clean()` in order to repeat phrases that were marked with a # words # pattern. These are described in detail below and in the final code. 

```{r}
repetitions <- function(string) {
  group <- string |>
  str_extract_all("([1-9])[^X]*\\1")
  #find the pattern we're looking for
  times <- group |>
  str_extract("[1-9]")
  #figure out the marking of how many times it should occur
  times <- as.numeric(times)
  #turn that marking into an actual number
  multiple <- strrep(group, times)
  #multiply that string by the multiple
  group <- string |>
  str_extract_all("([1-9])[^X]*\\1")
  #redefine the pattern we're looking for because group had to be renamed before (this is probably redundant but I'm confused rn so I don't wanna figure out the better way)
  string |>
    str_replace_all("([1-9])[^X]*\\1", multiple)
  #replace the initial string with what we want
}
enact_repeats <- function(string) {
  if_else(str_detect(string, "([1-9])[^X]*\\1"), repetitions(string), string)
}
#enact_repeats finds strings surrounded by numbers and enacts repetitions function (explained above)
clean <- function(string) {
  string |>
  str_replace_all("[1-9]X+[1-9]", "") |>
  #before anything, get rid of the #X# combinations cause that causes problems
  enact_repeats()|>
  str_replace_all("\\([^)]*\\)", "") |>
  #replace a ( followed by any number of any characters but a ) and then a )
  str_replace_all("<[^ ]*", "") |>
  #replace any < followed by any number of characters but space
  str_replace_all("[^ ]*>", "") |>
  #replace any number of characters but a space immediately before a >
  str_replace_all("_. |_", " ") |>
  #replace an underscore followed by a single character or an underscore by itself
  str_replace_all("~[^ ]*", "") |>
  #replace a tilde followed by any character but a space with an empty string
  str_remove_all("[\\[\\]+%@=*X\\)\\(]") |>
  #remove each of the symbols inside, all of them
  str_remove_all("\\.\\.+") |>
  #remove two or more literal dots, all of them
  str_replace_all("!(\\w)", "\\1") |>
  str_remove_all("--+") |>
  #remove two or more dashes, all of them
  str_replace_all("^ | $", "") |>
  #remove all spaces at the beginning or end of the line
  str_replace_all("[1-9]", " ") |>
  #replace spaces at the beginning and end of a line with no spaces
  str_replace_all("[ ]+", " ") |>
  #replace any space larger than one spaces with single spaces
  str_replace_all(" \\.", "\\.") |>
  str_replace_all(" \\,", "\\,") 
  #replaces any space before a period or comma with no space
}
```

Once each individual line was cleaned, the code below as implemented to get rid of white space, empty lines, and make sure only the `clean_words` column was selected. 

```{r}
trn_text <- clean_trn_wrds |>
  select(!words) |>
  #get rid of messy version of each line
  mutate(clean_words = trimws(clean_words)) |>
  #trim white space 
  filter(!clean_words == '') |>
  #filter out empty lines
  mutate(trn = "x",
         .before = clean_words)
  #add a column fill in for unifying these features
```

## Merging the text

With the text being clean, the last line of code in the previous chunk was added to prepare for the following code. 

```{r}
trn_text <- trn_text |>
  summarize(clean_words = str_flatten(clean_words, " "))
  #returns a single cell data frame of all of the dialogue combined with spaces
```

This successfully collapses the data frame into a single observation. 


## Making the id column

In order to make an id column that kept track of which .trn file was being observed, the code below was implemented. 

```{r}
trn <- str_extract(file, "\\d+")
#takes the thee numbers attached to each .trn

trn_df <- trn_text |>
  mutate(id = str_flatten(c("trn", trn), "_"),
         .before = "clean_words")
#creates a full name for each doc as trn_###
```


## The final Function and Iteration

```{r}
#creating a function to get the cleaned up words into a data frame all together
get_clean_wrds <- function(file) {

#reading in a file as a data frame

trn <- str_extract(file, "\\d+")
#takes the thee numbers attached to each .trn
  
trn_df <-  read_delim(file, col_names = FALSE)
#read in a file as a df

trn_wrds <- trn_df |>
  select(matches("X3|X4"))
  #we are selecting the third or fourth automatically named column. Most files will only select three, but some have a delimiting issue so there is an extra column (time stamps gets split)

#this function deals with the aformentioned data frames which still have two columns. If it detects two columns, it will automatically select the fourth one. Otherwise, it will proceed as normal
restrict_col <- function(df) {
  if (ncol(df) == 2) {
  #if the number of columns is exactly 2
    select(df, 2)}
    #select the second column
  else 
  #otherwise,
  {x}
    #just leave things the same
  }

trn_wrds <- restrict_col(trn_wrds) |>
  #limit columns to one as described in functions above
  select(words = 1)
#rename our column to words

# Function Definitions

#repetitions takes a given string and multiplies it by numbers that surround the string
repetitions <- function(string) {
  group <- string |>
  str_extract_all("([1-9])[^X]*\\1")
  #find the pattern we're looking for
  times <- group |>
  str_extract("[1-9]")
  #figure out the marking of how many times it should occur
  times <- as.numeric(times)
  #turn that marking into an actual number
  multiple <- strrep(group, times)
  #multiply that string by the multiple
  group <- string |>
  str_extract_all("([1-9])[^X]*\\1")
  #redefine the pattern we're looking for because group had to be renamed before (this is probably redundant but I'm confused rn so I don't wanna figure out the better way)
  string |>
    str_replace_all("([1-9])[^X]*\\1", multiple)
  #replace the initial string with what we want
}
enact_repeats <- function(string) {
  if_else(str_detect(string, "([1-9])[^X]*\\1"), repetitions(string), string)
}
#enact_repeats finds strings surrounded by numbers and enacts repetitions function (explained above)
clean <- function(string) {
  string |>
  str_replace_all("[1-9]X+[1-9]", "") |>
  #before anything, get rid of the #X# combinations cause that causes problems
  enact_repeats()|>
  str_replace_all("\\([^)]*\\)", "") |>
  #replace a ( followed by any number of any characters but a ) and then a )
  str_replace_all("<[^ ]*", "") |>
  #replace any < followed by any number of characters but space
  str_replace_all("[^ ]*>", "") |>
  #replace any number of characters but a space immediately before a >
  str_replace_all("_. |_", " ") |>
  #replace an underscore followed by a single character or an underscore by itself
  str_replace_all("~[^ ]*", "") |>
  #replace a tilde followed by any character but a space with an empty string
  str_remove_all("[\\[\\]+%@=*X\\)\\(]") |>
  #remove each of the symbols inside, all of them
  str_remove_all("\\.\\.+") |>
  #remove two or more literal dots, all of them
  str_replace_all("!(\\w)", "\\1") |>
  str_remove_all("--+") |>
  #remove two or more dashes, all of them
  str_replace_all("^ | $", "") |>
  #remove all spaces at the beginning or end of the line
  str_replace_all("[1-9]", " ") |>
  #replace spaces at the beginning and end of a line with no spaces
  str_replace_all("[ ]+", " ") |>
  #replace any space larger than one spaces with single spaces
  str_replace_all(" \\.", "\\.") |>
  str_replace_all(" \\,", "\\,") 
  #replaces any space before a period or comma with no space
}
#clean cleans up a data frame column made up of transcription markings to make it as close as possible to only dialogue. 

#Using clean() to clean up a data frame

clean_trn_wrds <- trn_wrds |>
  mutate(clean_words = clean(words))

#Getting the rows of dialogue into a single cell of dialogue

trn_text <- clean_trn_wrds |>
  select(!words) |>
  #get rid of messy version of each line
  mutate(clean_words = trimws(clean_words)) |>
  #trim white space 
  filter(!clean_words == '') |>
  #filter out empty lines
  mutate(trn = "x",
         .before = clean_words)
  #add a column fill in for unifying these features

trn_text <- trn_text |>
  summarize(clean_words = str_flatten(clean_words, " "))
  #returns a single cell data frame of all of the dialogue combined with spaces

trn_df <- trn_text |>
  mutate(id = str_flatten(c("trn", trn), "_"),
         .before = "clean_words")
  #creates a full name for each doc as trn_###

trn_df
}
```

The code below was used to create a list of every file name from the zip folder. 

```{r}
files = list.files("SBCorpus/TRN", full.names = TRUE)
#here we go into the file TRN and pull out all of the full names for the files
files
```

And finally, the code below was used to map this function onto every file in the files list. 

```{r}
list_files <- files |>
  map(get_clean_wrds) 

all_trns <- do.call(rbind, list_files)

all_trns
```
